subject: EU-only data controls & evidence for SCCs — backup and deletion proof
messages:
From: Marta Kozlov <marta.kozlov@horizonhealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: EU-only processing — evidence we can rely on

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the overview earlier. Before we progress to legal sign-off we need a clear written response on two narrow points from Redwood's side: 

1) Can you confirm that Horizon tenant data (including embeddings, search indexes, and audit logs) will never be accessible from a US-based Redwood service or subprocessor? Our requirement is EU-only processing and that means no fallback/backup copies in the US.

2) For deletion requests (subject access / customer-directed deletion), can you provide an example of the deletion evidence you provide to customers? Specifically: deletion timestamps, which replicas were destroyed, and any audit logs that show the lifecycle.

We'd appreciate links or attachments to standard playbooks/pdfs you can share. Ivan (our counsel) will loop in if we need additional clarifications.

Best,
Marta
Security Program Manager
Horizon Health

Subject: Re: EU-only processing — evidence we can rely on

Hi Marta — great questions, thank you. High level answers below and I attached the questionnaire you sent with our inline notes.

1) EU-only processing: Yes — Redwood can be configured so that all active inference and storage for a given tenant is pinned to EU regions (we typically use eu-west-1 and eu-central-1). We do not route customer requests or KV cache snapshots to US-hosted inference nodes when EU-only is selected. That said, there are a couple of areas we should confirm with legal/security: backups and some long-term disaster recovery (DR) artifacts. I will have Rishi and Laura add technical/legal specifics below.

2) Deletion evidence: We provide a deletion report that includes deletion request id, timestamp (UTC), list of storage buckets/volumes/indices where objects were removed, and KMS key metadata used to encrypt the objects. The audit trail includes API call IDs and internal job IDs. See attached deletion_playbook_v1 for the format we share.

Next steps: Laura, can you confirm SCCs wording around subprocessors and an explicit commitment on backup geography? Rishi — can you attach the data-flow diagram and a short note on backups, key management, and log retention? Marta / Ivan — we can schedule a 30-minute call Monday to walk through the attachments.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Marta / Ivan / Aisha,

Thank you for raising these points. To be explicit on the contractual side: the Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) we propose will include the subprocessor table and an explicit clause that subprocessor transfers outside the EEA require prior notice and the right to object. For backups, our standard SCCs reference that transient copies for DR are permitted only within agreed jurisdictions; we can add an explicit EU-only backup residency commitment for Horizon as a bespoke addendum to the SCCs.

On deletion evidence: the playbook Aisha referenced is the format we normally produce. If Horizon requires a signed attestation-level report (for example, a time-bound certificate that certain shards/replicas were securely destroyed) we can discuss a scoped attestation with security. That would typically be handled as an add-on (procedural evidence).

Ivan — can you confirm whether Horizon's procurement needs a formal attestation vs. the standard deletion report? If yes, we will scope with Security for what level of on-prem-style destruction logs we can deliver.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marta Kozlov <marta.kozlov@horizonhealth.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 11:35:00 -0500
Subject: Re: EU-only processing — evidence we can rely on

Hi all — adding the technical detail you asked for. TL;DR: EU-only mode uses region-locked S3 equivalents (eu buckets), local KMS CMKs in the same region, and isolated GPU serving pools pinned to EU availability zones. A few specifics: 

- Active storage and inference: pinned to eu-west-1 or eu-central-1. No cross-region read by default.
- Backups/DR: We operate daily snapshot backups and a weekly cross-AZ archive. For enterprise EU-only customers we can restrict backups to EU regions only. Our backup orchestration runs in the same region and uses encryption-at-rest with locally managed keys.
- Subprocessors: We currently use a EU-based monitoring vendor for metrics ingestion for EU customers; the central logging aggregator (for platform ops) is in EU for EU-only tenants. Some vendor services (support tooling, ticket routing) are SaaS and may have metadata endpoints in the US — we can minimize this and exclude sensitive payloads. We'll surface the subprocessor list in the SCCs table.
- Deletion process: deletion request kicks off an async job: 1) mark tenant objects for deletion in metadata store; 2) background worker deletes objects from primary storage and index shards; 3) snapshot manager enqueues replica deletion; 4) KMS key rotation or rewrap performed as required. Audit log entries are written to write-once logs (immutable append-only) with API call IDs and internal job IDs.

Attachments: I attached a simplified data-flow diagram showing EU-only flows and a redwood deletion_playbook_v1.docx that includes a sample deletion report template that shows per-replica deletion timestamps and job ids.

Notes & caveats:
- If Horizon wants a contractual promise to never transfer any data to the US under any failure scenario (including multi-region DR failover), we need to model that operationally and add specific SLA/commitments; some extreme DR scenarios may require scoped exception language.
- For attestation-level evidence (signed destruction certificates), we will need a scoping call to confirm what evidence is acceptable to Horizon, and there may be delivery lead time.

Happy to jump on a call Monday (I can do 09:00-12:00 CET).

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Security & Infrastructure | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-eu-data-flow-diagram.png, deletion_playbook_v1.docx

Laura / Rishi / Aisha,

Quick clarifying questions from counsel: 

1) For the deletion report template — will the report include immutable log hashes or signatures that can be submitted to regulators as tamper-evidence? Examples: SHA256 of the write-once log blocks, or signed log snapshots.
2) For backups — please confirm whether long-term cold backups (retention > 90 days) are ever exported to a US region for archival, even under 'EU-only' tenancy. We need an explicit negative for Horizon to sign the SCCs without exceptions.

If Redwood can provide (a) a negative commitment on US export for backup/cold archives and (b) tamper-evident logs in the deletion report, Horizon will likely accept the SCCs addendum. If not, we will draft fallback language.

Regards,
Ivan Petrov
Counsel, Horizon Health

Hi Marta / Ivan — thanks for the precision here. Summary and proposed next steps: 

1) US export of backups: We can commit contractually that cold backups and archival exports for Horizon will be restricted to EEA regions only. That will be added as a bespoke clause in the SCCs addendum (Laura to draft). Operationally, this requires us to pin backup buckets and archival jobs to EU-only storage classes — Rishi has confirmed this is feasible.

2) Tamper-evident deletion logs: We can supply SHA256 digests of the write-once audit logs and include signed snapshots as part of the deletion report package. This will be delivered as part of the standard deletion report for Horizon. If Horizon requires a formal third-party attestation, we will scope that separately.

Deliverables (action owners & ETA):
- Laura: SCCs addendum language & subprocessor table for EU-only commitment — draft by Thu, 18 Nov 2026.
- Rishi: Export a sample deletion report (with SHA256 hashes) and the redwood-eu-data-flow-diagram — by Wed, 17 Nov 2026.
- Aisha: Schedule a 30-min technical walk-through with Horizon & Ivan for Fri, 19 Nov 2026 10:00 CET (proposed).

I've attached the filled questionnaire and the playbook as promised. Please confirm the call time or propose alternatives.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
